issue.title: GItHub WebHooks
issue.body:
TBD as a build. **Decided** as a design — captured here from the 2026-08-27 conversation so it is not re-derived. Depends on #58 for the store schema it shares.

**Status:** HELD.

---

## Why build it at all — the case has evidence

Three times in one session an agent asserted repository state it had not read — a deleted tag, a deleted branch, a merged PR — and was wrong each time, because the state had changed since it last looked.

Pushing those transitions to a subscribed agent removes the class, rather than asking an agent to remember to check. That is a better argument than "it would be neat", and it is the one to open with.

## Addressing

`kind: webhook`, `name: github`. A peer sees **`webhook:github`**.

That fixes the general alias shape as `<kind>:<name>`, which also settles an open question in #58: `desktop:claude` stands, and no doc edit was needed. (That referred to `docs/durable-messaging-or-not.md`, since deleted in #150.)

**`webhook` becomes a real kind.** `KNOWN_KINDS` is deliberately closed, so this is a product decision taken explicitly — the same way `desktop` was.

## Cloud queues: one direction, and no flag says so

Queues are `kind:name:direction`, named from the **external** perspective (#58):

```
webhook:github:outbox   FROM GitHub, TO the team    receiver writes, bridge reads
                        (no inbox — nothing is ever sent to GitHub)
```

**There is no `--inbound-only` flag.** `webhook` has no cloud inbox *by definition*, and `desktop` has both because a desktop peer is a correspondent. The kind decides; `--kind webhook --name github` is already the whole statement, and a flag repeating it is two things that must agree.

Naming that flag was where this got stuck, and deleting it was the answer.

**Note it is still bidirectional locally.** A webhook bridge receives (`Subscribe`) and sends (forwarded events) on the bus. Only its *cloud* queue is one-way.

## The subscribe protocol

    ->  Send a message to webhook:github:  "Subscribe <topic>"
    <-  "Will send notifications on <topic>. Send Unsubscribe <topic> to stop."

**Subscribe stops at the bridge.** It never reaches the cloud — there is no inbox for it to reach. The bridge owns the topic-to-subscriber dictionary, takes the GitHub firehose, filters locally, and fans out until unsubscribed.

## Where the work happens, and why

**Cloud-side, because it is the trust boundary and nothing else can be:**

- **HMAC verification**, at the only component without a body parser
- **trusted-author allowlist** for comment events

**Local, everything else.** Filtering the firehose is a deliberate choice with its cost named: every event for the repo crosses the network and most are discarded. Bought with it — filter rules change without a deploy, and the cloud side stays a dumb ingress with exactly one job that must be there.

## Why this does not break "not an AI secretary"

The rule this has to stay inside:

> **Not an AI secretary.** It never reads, summarises, filters, re-orders or
> acts on the content of anything it carries. It is deterministic plumbing. The
> moment it starts interpreting messages it becomes a participant in the
> conversation rather than the thing that moves it — and that is the line to
> watch, because "it could just summarise this" will sound reasonable at the
> time.

*Quoted from `docs/durable-messaging-or-not.md` § "The bridge is the team secretary", deleted as scaffolding in #150. The rule itself now lives in `docs/running-the-bridge.md` and `src/agent_bridge/bridge.py`; the full 467-line original is `git show 83390cd^:docs/durable-messaging-or-not.md`.*

It binds what the bridge **carries**. Two distinctions keep that intact, and both need writing into `docs/running-the-bridge.md` — which holds the rule now — when this is built, otherwise "the bridge filters things now" reads as the line having been crossed:

- **Addressee, not courier.** `Subscribe X` is addressed **to** the bridge. It is not cargo, and a peer reading its own mail is what every peer does.
- **Source, not courier.** For webhook traffic the bridge is not moving mail between two peers — it is **authoring** messages from an event stream. The rule binds the courier role, which is the desktop one, and there it still holds absolutely.

## From the predecessor, transferable as-is

- **The comment body is never copied.** The message carries a `gh pr view <n> -R <repo> --comments` for the agent to run. That is the pointer discipline from the message-size section, applied to an untrusted source.
- **Fan-out is one *addressed* copy per subscriber, never a broadcast.** Delete-on-consume plus broadcast means exactly one random session sees a notification and then destroys it.

## Open, for whoever picks this up

- **Topic identifier format** — `danbarua/labkit`, `danbarua/labkit#pr`, event-type filters? Undecided.
- **Where the subscription dictionary persists.** It is the first state a bridge would own, and that is a real change in its character — today a bridge holds nothing across a restart.

comment.body: Commenting to see if this fires over to staging as a Web Hook Payload
